newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BMW says Jan-Feb sales surge 17 percent.
newsitem.headline: BMW says Jan-Feb sales surge 17 percent.

text.p: German carmaker BMW AG said Tuesday that sales in January and February were up 17 percent to more than 100,000 vehicles over the 1996 period.

But the Munich-based carmaker also said sales at its Rover group in Britain were not up to year-ago levels during the two-month period, in part due to the introduction of two new models, including the Rover 200.
BMW Management Board Chairman Bernd Pischetsrieder, in a speech to be delivered at a BMW event at the Geneva car show, said the carmaker expected a "stable development" in BMW sales at higher levels.
In 1996, BMW saw record demand for its vehicles and set new production and sales levels.
Pischetsrieder said he expected vehicle demand in industrialised nations to be limited to the replacement of existing vehicles.
In Europe, he said little growth in real income and tax law changes would lead to slight growth for the industry. He also forecast stagnant markets in Japan and North America.
